liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Not Fade Away** (1 review, 2 other sources): Reviewer says the second set started great but faded after Not Fade Away; the third set is essential for collectors; John Cippolina sat in, and a Goin' Down The Road tease followed the song [1][2][23]
- **Baby What You Want Me To Do** (1 review, 1 other source): Attendee's favorite; the crowd danced wildly while Etta James looked on, apparently unused to such a scene; Not played since September 7, 1969, according to the notes [3][18]
- **C C Rider** (1 review): Matt Kelly turns it loose, steering the band back to its blues roots [19]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): After the first verse Bobby exclaims in surprise at all the balloons [20]

## Setlist highlights

- **Midnight Madness**: back after 325 archived shows (1461 days); rare: 7 archived performances [26]
- **Tell Mama**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [26]
- **Baby What You Want Me To Do**: back after 970 archived shows (4863 days); rare: 5 archived performances [26]
- **In The Midnight Hour**: back after 800 archived shows (4264 days) [26]
- **31/82 Set 3**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [26]
- **Tell Mama**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [26]
- **Baby What You Want Me To Do**: back after 970 archived shows (4863 days); rare: 5 archived performances [26]

## The recordings

- **gd1982-12-31.sbd.miller.77301.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 30 songs; 190 min; rated 3.58/5 by 12 [1]
- **gd1982-12-31.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.105820.flac16**: soundboard; 25 songs; 165 min [2]
- **gd1982-12-31.148505.mat.tobin.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 25 songs; 164 min [3]
- **gd82-12-31.sbd.bode.5958.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 152 min; rated 4.16/5 by 19 [8]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says third set has dropouts and Garcia's guitar is often buried in this soundboard mix, despite his strong playing; Clean soundboard, but Garcia's guitar is buried, notably in the jam into Not Fade Away, along with Cipollina's whammy-bar effects; Reviewer calls the sound good and clean [15][16][17][19]
- **gd1982-12-31.134487.s3.nak300.schley.flac2448**: audience recording; 6 songs; 36 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [11]

## Around the show

- Attendee recalls long waiting for tickets until Bill Graham finally came out with them; the event felt bigger than the band [18]
- Rock Scully's book reportedly says Etta James barely made it, was sent a limo, and found the band tripping; she praised Garcia's playing [19]
- Attendee waited hours after the show to retrieve a jacket, then reached Haight after 3 am, feeling tired and out of place [21]
- Etta James said the Dead are the best blues band; the odd sounds opening Sugar Magnolia were the end of the countdown [23]
- Reviewer was born on this date, about ten hours before the show's events [25]
- Matthew Kelly joined for Baby What You Want Me To Do and C C Rider; the third set featured Etta James and Tower of Power [1]
- Etta James and the Tower of Power Horns played the third set; Matt Kelly sat in on several songs [2]
- Etta James sang in set 3 with Tower of Power Horns; Stephen Doc Kupka played baritone sax [3]
- Reviewer had a warmer audience-blended tape without dropouts and believes the pre-FM version is a better mix [15]
- Garcia and Cipollina are more prominent on a show fragment that circulated around the Bay Area in the 1980s [16]
- Reviewer says the show falls short of the previous year's New Year's Eve, though it has great moments [23]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1982-12-31.sbd.miller.77301.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Cassettes provided by Joani Walker and Paul Scotton; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Nakamichi 550/Maxell XLIIS-90) [1]
- **gd1982-12-31.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.105820.flac16**: taped by Paul Scotton and Joani Walker; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Nakamichi 550/Maxell XLIIS-90) [2]. Also: Transfer is from Walker and Scotton cassettes, per the file name [2]
- **gd1982-12-31.148505.mat.tobin.flac16**: transferred by SBD + AUD Matrix 2 Source Mix (44/16) by Kevin Tobin; source: SBD + AUD Matrix 2 Source Mix (44/16) [3]. Also: This is a mix made by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC in December 2019 [3]
- **gd82-12-31.sbd.bode.5958.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Charlie Miller and Keith Bode; source: Soundboard [8]. Also: Reviewer says a good audience recording exists and urges its holder to upload it [22]
- **gd1982-12-31.134487.s3.nak300.schley.flac2448**: taped by Brian Schley; transferred by Andrew F.; source: 3rd Set AUD: Nakamichi CM300/CP4 shotguns > Sony TC-D5 > Hitachi ME Metal tape. Set up FOB, recording by Brian Schley. [11]. Also: Taken from a Schley Nak 300 source; the other two tapes of this show are currently lost [11]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Gregg Nixon Grateful Dead: [1982-12-31 Oakland Auditorium Arena, Oakland, CA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1982-12-31-oakland-auditorium-arena-oakland-ca-usa/) [27]
